# Architecture decision records

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask adr index --write` from the ADR files in this directory. Do not edit: the tidy rule `adr-index-doc` fails when this file is stale. -->

The rules for how nami is written, tested, merged and paid for, and why. The process is defined in ADR-0000, amended by ADR-20261128-1856. Accepted ADRs are not edited; a new ADR supersedes them. The exceptions are the status line, links, and a mechanical change that is applied to every ADR and recorded in the ADR that makes it (ADR-0015, ADR-20261128-1856). Only a human can accept an ADR. Agents may propose them.

**A new ADR** starts with `cargo xtask adr new <slug>`. Its ID is the UTC minute it was started, `ADR-YYYYMMDD-HHMM`, and its file is `YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<slug>.md`. ADRs 0000 to 0043 keep their numbers. Each row below comes from one ADR: its title, its `- Status:` line and its `- Summary:` line. An ADR that changes another says so in a `- Amends: ADR-…` line, which fills the other's Amended by column. After changing any of these, run `cargo xtask adr index --write`.

Dev and tooling crates are allow-listed. Anything new needs an ADR. |

No allocation after init. Data access only via pencils, `[f64; NVAR]` and typed gathers. |

Overflow checks stay on in release. |

Claims are lock files on a `claims` branch, managed via `cargo xtask task`. |

| [0015](0015-crate-names-and-review-gated-paths.md) | Unprefixed crate names, "references", and protected paths gated at review | Accepted | [0019](0019-the-stop-gate.md) (proposed), [0020](0020-guardrails-that-grow.md) (proposed), [0022](0022-guardrail-rule-changes-merge-on-proof.md) (proposed) | Crates are named after their directory, with no `nami-` prefix. "Oracle" becomes "reference". Agents may edit protected paths; code-owner review gates the merge. |
| [0017](0017-passes-set-by-ci.md) | CI sets `passes` through the bot's PR | Accepted (2026-11-28, by the maintainer) |  | A post-merge workflow runs each task's acceptance tests on `main`, and the `nami-ci` bot opens the one PR that sets `passes`; `check-pr` rejects every other change that does. |
| [0018](0018-rule-registry-and-checked-tags.md) | One rule registry, enforcement tags that tidy checks, and the gaps they exposed | Proposed |  | Every tidy rule is registered and has a firing and a non-firing fixture. A tag in the style guide names a mechanism that exists. Planned mechanisms are listed and each is a task. |
| [0019](0019-the-stop-gate.md) | The stop hook is a gate, and sessions start with working tools | Proposed | [0033](0033-fewer-degrees-of-freedom.md) (proposed) | The stop hook runs `just check dylint` unless the tree equals `main` or the last green run, and blocks three times. A session-start hook fixes `PATH` and checks tool versions. |
| [0020](0020-guardrails-that-grow.md) | Guardrails that grow: learnings, the pull-request record and the base gate | Proposed | [0021](0021-follow-ups-are-issues.md) (proposed), [0022](0022-guardrail-rule-changes-merge-on-proof.md) (proposed) | Agents add guardrails at the lowest rung that works, or record a learning. The PR description lists protected files and guardrail gaps. The base branch's tidy runs on every PR's tree. |
| [0021](0021-follow-ups-are-issues.md) | Follow-ups are GitHub issues, claimed like tasks | Proposed (point 6 Accepted, 2026-11-26, by the maintainer) | [0023](0023-bot-keys-in-ci.md) (proposed) | A finding outside the task is filed as an issue and fixed by another session, which claims it on the `claims` branch. Agents act only on issues by the bot or a code owner, and on the CI app's queue-failure issues in the shape that ADR-0023 checks (point 2, amended by ADR-0023). A merge-queue failure is fixed on the failing PR's own branch (point 6, whose vocabulary ADR-0023 extends to `guardrails.yml`). The bot lifts its own `needs-decision` after it records a code owner's decision (point 7). |
| [0022](0022-guardrail-rule-changes-merge-on-proof.md) | Guardrail rule changes merge on proof | Proposed |  | Rule paths (what a tidy rule or dylint lint reports, its fixtures and UI cases) have no code owner. The base's `cargo xtask ratchet`, a required check, proves without running the PR's code in the judging job that every case the base writes down still holds, the rule tables only tighten and mutation testing misses nothing. An additive change (new rules beside the old code) then merges on that proof, unless the reviewer app has an open request for changes or thread; an edit to existing rule code also needs the reviewer app's approval of the head commit, or a code owner's. |
| [0023](0023-bot-keys-in-ci.md) | Bot keys in CI | Proposed |  | One GitHub App per role: `nami-agent` for authoring, `nami-reviewer` for the CI-hosted review, `nami-ci` for CI jobs, whom agents trust only for the shapes it produces. A key lives in an environment that only `main` may use. Each job narrows its tokens, one step holds the secret, and no job with a key runs PR code or restores a cache. |
| [0032](0032-agents-run-in-a-sandbox.md) | Agents run in a sandbox | Proposed |  | On the maintainer's machine, every agent session in a nami checkout runs in a bubblewrap sandbox without the maintainer's credentials, and a tripwire hook denies sessions outside it. Nothing in the repository depends on it. It stops mistakes, not attackers. No agent sessions on macOS until it has an equivalent. |
| [0033](0033-fewer-degrees-of-freedom.md) | Fewer degrees of freedom: one strict lint level, nightly rustfmt, and tests that agents cannot quietly weaken | Proposed |  | One lint level for every crate, with nami-only lints in checked crate headers. One form for each choice, the other banned. Nightly rustfmt. Tests change only with a code owner's label. |
| [0034](0034-purpose-users-and-success-criteria.md) | Purpose, users and success criteria | Proposed |  | nami is a production MHD solver: safe, at least as fast as Athena++/AthenaK, flexible enough to outgrow AthenaK, built swarm-first. Failure is unreadable code or significantly worse performance. |
| [0035](0035-scope-and-roadmap.md) | Scope and roadmap | Proposed |  | One block-based, coordinate-aware data model from M0. Compile-time extension points. Advection, Burgers, Euler, shallow water, then MHD, curvilinear, multiple nodes, SMR, AMR. |
| [0036](0036-numerics.md) | Numerical methods | Proposed |  | Standard methods with Athena++'s menu as the yardstick. Positivity from named, counted components, never silent floors. Every selectable combination is verified. Interfaces allow subcycling and fourth order. |
| [0037](0037-extension-points-and-composition.md) | Extension points and how a run is composed | Proposed |  | A run is a combination compiled in a problem crate; runtime configuration sets parameters. Riemann solvers work in the face frame. Integrators are 3S* tables. Every supported combination is tested. |
| [0038](0038-mesh-blocks-and-time-loop.md) | Mesh, blocks and the time loop | Proposed |  | Blocks of one size in a linear Morton-key octree. Fixed-capacity pools from a memory budget, even under AMR. A fixed list of phases per stage, bulk-synchronous until M7. A `mesh` crate that `kernels` never sees. |
| [0039](0039-parallelism-and-communication.md) | Parallelism and communication | Proposed |  | Auto-vectorisation only; one process per NUMA domain with static threads; own `Transport` (in-process, TCP, InfiniBand), launched by Slurm. Results are bitwise identical for any decomposition. |
| [0040](0040-infiniband-binding-crate.md) | A binding crate for InfiniBand | Proposed |  | A crate `fabric` binds `libibverbs` behind the off-by-default feature `infiniband`, with `unsafe` confined to it. Amends 0001 and 0014 points 2 to 4 (a second crate with `unsafe`, a second `#[expect]`, the first `unsafe` in runtime code) once accepted. |
| [0041](0041-interface-output-and-guarantees.md) | Interface, output and determinism guarantees | Proposed |  | Problem binaries with `run`, `check` and `restart`; a strict TOML subset with no defaults; own binary format with version metadata; restart refuses a different build. Bitwise across platforms, decompositions and restarts. |
| [0042](0042-verification-strategy.md) | Verification strategy | Proposed |  | Check suites chosen by declared properties, owned by `reference`. An outside anchor per system, Athena++ as a second source of reference data, bitwise architecture tests, a split gate, thresholds as Rust constants. Amends 0007 and 0001 once accepted. |
| [0043](0043-data-layout-and-kernel-shape.md) | Data layout and kernel shape | Proposed |  | Structure of arrays `[var][k][j][i]`, kernels on row stencils, per-face physics over named state structs. Measured at 1.9× Athena++ only with `f64::sqrt`, which today's rules ban, and `debug_assert!` in `math::sqrt` (with a copy of today's `math::sqrt`: 0.1×, below the 0.8× failure line, or 0.9×, below the 1.0× target, depending on inlining). Amends 0003 once accepted. |
| [20261128-1856](20261128-1856-adr-ids-are-utc-minutes.md) | ADR IDs are UTC minutes, and the index is generated | Proposed |  | A new ADR's ID is the UTC minute it was started, `ADR-YYYYMMDD-HHMM`, and `cargo xtask adr new <slug>` writes it; 0000 to 0043 keep their numbers. Every `ADR-` reference resolves, the clash check fails a same-minute clash, and `docs/design/README.md` is generated from each ADR's header. |
